description: Project-level dashboard for ai-delivery-assistant. Data limitation, stated plainly: the application exposes its numbers as authenticated JSON (GET /api/metrics) and does not expose Prometheus text-format metrics at any path. The Prometheus job ai-delivery-assistant (monitoring/prometheus.yml) scrapes http://app:8000/metrics, a route api.py does not define, so the SPA fallback route answers it and scrape_samples_scraped stays 0. Every panel here therefore uses only metrics Prometheus produces for its own scrape targets: up, scrape_duration_seconds, scrape_samples_scraped. Rows for status distribution, resolution rate and per-project counts carry their unavailable application data as documented text with the exact JSON keys and the endpoint that holds them, because inventing metric names would be worse than showing nothing.

Status distribution
panels.description: Count of projects per delivery status. The app computes this in GET /api/metrics as JSON behind authentication; Prometheus holds no series for it, so this row documents the data instead of faking a metric.

No Prometheus series backs this row. The panel states which endpoint holds the data and the exact keys it returns, so the row can be rebuilt as soon as the app exposes Prometheus text format or a JSON API datasource is provisioned.

options.content:
**Data not available from Prometheus.**

The app computes project status counts only in the authenticated JSON endpoint `GET /api/metrics`, response key `status_distribution`, an array of objects:

- `status`: human-readable delivery status, one of "on track", "at risk", "off track", "delivered", "blocked", "unknown" (the app stores snake_case values and replaces underscores with spaces)
- `count`: number of projects with that status

`GET /api/metrics` requires a bearer token (`Depends(get_current_user)` in api.py), and the job `ai-delivery-assistant` scrapes `/metrics`, a route api.py does not define: the SPA fallback route answers it. Prometheus therefore holds no project status series and no panel on this row can be backed by real data.

To make this row real:

1. Expose the counts in Prometheus text format at `/metrics` (for example `aida_project_status{status="on track"} 4`), which the job already scrapes; or
2. Provision a JSON API datasource (Grafana Infinity) and point the panel at `GET /api/metrics`.

This dashboard cannot do it with the single Prometheus datasource that `monitoring/grafana/datasources/prometheus.yml` provisions.

panels.title: Status distribution: application JSON only, not Prometheus
Resolution rate
panels.description: Share of risks, blockers and action items that are no longer open. The app returns it as a float from GET /api/metrics; no Prometheus series carries it, so this row documents the data instead of faking a metric.

No Prometheus series backs this row. The panel states which endpoint holds the data and the exact keys it returns, so the row can be rebuilt as soon as the app exposes Prometheus text format or a JSON API datasource is provisioned.

options.content:
**Data not available from Prometheus.**

`GET /api/metrics` returns `resolution_rate`: a float, the share of every recorded risk, blocker and action item that is resolved or completed. An empty ledger reads as 1.0. The backing counts are in the same response under `totals`:

- `resolved_risks`, `resolved_blockers`, `resolved_actions`
- `open_risks`, `open_blockers`, `open_actions`

None of these values exist in Prometheus, because the app has no Prometheus text-format endpoint at `/metrics`. The scrape target for job `ai-delivery-assistant` exposes no samples at all: `scrape_samples_scraped` is 0.

To make this row real:

1. Publish a gauge such as `aida_resolution_rate` plus counters for the six totals through `/metrics`; or
2. Provision a JSON API datasource (Grafana Infinity) and plot `resolution_rate` from `GET /api/metrics`.

A number here that was not read from one of those two sources would be invented, so this row shows the contract instead.

panels.title: Resolution rate: application JSON only, not Prometheus
Per-project counts
panels.description: Meetings and open risks, blockers and action items per project. The app returns them from GET /api/metrics and GET /api/dashboard as JSON behind authentication; no Prometheus series carries them, so this row documents the data instead of faking a metric.

No Prometheus series backs this row. The panel states which endpoint holds the data and the exact keys it returns, so the row can be rebuilt as soon as the app exposes Prometheus text format or a JSON API datasource is provisioned.

options.content:
**Data not available from Prometheus.**

`GET /api/metrics` returns `per_project`: one object per project with these keys:

- `project_id`, `name`
- `meetings`: Meeting rows for the project
- `open_risks`, `open_blockers`, `open_actions`: items with status "open"

`GET /api/dashboard` returns a similar per-project shape plus `status`, `progress`, `open_risks`, `open_blockers`, `open_actions`, `meeting_count` and `last_meeting`.

Both endpoints require a bearer token, and neither is in Prometheus text format. Prometheus scrapes `/metrics`, which the app does not implement, so there is no series with a project label to group by.

To make this row real:

1. Emit one counter per project through `/metrics` with a project label (for example `aida_open_risks{project="Platform"} 3`); or
2. Provision a JSON API datasource (Grafana Infinity) and point a table panel at `GET /api/dashboard`.

The application statuses behind these counts, from the code: risks and blockers move between "open" and "resolved", action items between "open" and "completed", and risk impact is "high", "medium", "low" or "unknown".
